children: Tempus AI is launching a multiyear research initiative to build a multimodal dataset of 100,000 whole genomes, with the goal of improving artificial-intelligence medical research.
The company said the effort will build on its work establishing a real-world oncology database and structuring the data for use in training AI models.

"Now, Tempus is expanding beyond targeted gene panels into WGS to create a deeper understanding of the role the genome plays in disease progression and treatment response, all toward the goal of improving patient outcomes," the company said Friday.
Once the initial project is complete, Tempus said it plans to expand the dataset to eventually include 1 million genomes.

The dataset will be integrated into Tempus's existing data environment and is designed specifically to build and validate AI models, the company said. The initial dataset is available through the company's Early Adopter Program, with new members expected to be onboarded in phases until the platform is generally available next year.

"Tempus has spent the last decade building the infrastructure to connect diagnostics, multimodal clinical data and AI at scale," Chief Executive Eric Lefkofsky said. "Adding whole genome data linked to longitudinal outcomes makes that platform even more powerful and gives researchers a richer foundation to build AI models, generate new insights and ultimately improve patient care."
